- **Soap** [`soap`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soap.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Soap boilers make soft tallow-and-potash soap for laundry; hard Venetian soap is imported. In the siege tallow is wanted for candles. Local: Seifensieder (soap boilers, also chandlers).
- **Distillation of strong alcohol (aqua vitae)** [`distillation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/distillation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high Local: apothecaries; brandy distillers (Branntweiner); monastery pharmacies.
- **Sulphuric acid (oil of vitriol)** [`sulphuric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sulphuric_acid.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Oil of vitriol is distilled in small glass retorts from green vitriol or made under a glass bell from burning sulphur. Quantities are ounces, not barrels. Local: apothecaries; imperial mint; vitriol from the Hungarian mining towns.
- **Oxygen and combustion** [`oxygen_combustion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oxygen_combustion.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. The learned account is Becher's: bodies burn by losing a fatty earth (terra pinguis). Becher served Leopold I in Vienna in the 1670s and died in 1682. Elsewhere: Oxford: Mayow's nitro-aerial spirit (1674), little noticed.
- **Nitric acid (aqua fortis)** [`nitric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nitric_acid.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Scheidewasser is routine for parting gold from silver. It competes with gunpowder for saltpetre, which the arsenal claims first in a siege. Local: imperial mint; goldsmiths and assayers.
- **Saltpetre from nitre beds** [`saltpetre_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/saltpetre_production.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Privileged saltpetre men scrape stables, cellars and old walls and refine with wood ash. Beds take a year or more to ripen. A powder store burns on 31 August. Local: Saliterer (saltpetre men); imperial and civic arsenals.
- **Chemical elements and conservation of mass** [`chemical_elements`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chemical_elements.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Chymists reason with salt, sulphur and mercury, the schools with four elements. Boyle's Sceptical Chymist exists in Latin. Nobody weighs everything before and after.
- **Atomic theory and fixed proportions** [`atomic_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomic_theory.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Gassendi's and Boyle's corpuscles are known. Jesuit censors watch atomism because of the Eucharist. Proof by combining weights needs purer reagents and better balances than exist.

- **Gas laws (pressure, volume, temperature)** [`gas_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_laws.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Guericke showed his pump at Regensburg in 1654, and the Jesuit Schott printed the experiments. Boyle's and Mariotte's rule is in books; nobody here has built a pump. Elsewhere: Hamburg: Otto von Guericke (dies 1686); London: Boyle, Hooke; Paris: Mariotte, Huygens, Papin's work.
- **Collecting and telling apart gases (hydrogen, fixed air)** [`pneumatic_chemistry_gases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pneumatic_chemistry_gases.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Van Helmont's word 'gas' is known; airs are thought to be one air more or less tainted. Vintners know that fermenting cellars kill and test them with a candle.
- **Acids, alkalis and indicators** [`acids_bases_ph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/acids_bases_ph.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Apothecaries know that acids fizz with alkalis, and syrup of violets changing colour is in Boyle (1664). Physicians of the new school explain all disease by acid and alkali.
- **Hydrochloric acid and aqua regia** [`hydrochloric_acid_aqua_regia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydrochloric_acid_aqua_regia.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Spirit of salt is made by Glauber's method from salt and oil of vitriol; aqua regia from aqua fortis and sal ammoniac dissolves gold for assayers and gilders. Local: apothecaries; imperial mint; goldsmiths.
- **Alkalis (potash, soda, caustic lye)** [`alkali_soda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alkali_soda.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Potash is leached from wood ash of the surrounding forests; soda ash comes through Venice. The two are not told apart as substances.
- **Lime burning and lime mortar** [`lime_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lime_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Kilns and limestone lie outside the walls toward the Wienerwald. During the siege repairs to the bastions use stored lime, earth, timber and woolsacks.
- **Salt making (sea salt, brine boiling, rock salt)** [`salt_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/salt_production.md) — K4, use correct, make hard, accept high. No brine near Vienna. Salt is a sovereign monopoly and comes down the Danube from the Salzkammergut; the besieged city lives on its stock. Local: Salzamt and the landing on the Salzgries. Elsewhere: Hallstatt, Ischl, Aussee, Hallein, Hall in Tirol.
- **Dyeing with mordants and vat dyes** [`mordant_dyeing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mordant_dyeing.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Dyers work with alum, madder and woad; indigo and cochineal are bought through Venice and the Dutch.
- **Chlorine, bleaching powder and disinfection** [`chlorine_bleach`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chlorine_bleach.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Spirit of salt at the apothecary and the glassmakers' Braunstein are both obtainable; nobody has heated them together. Plague goods are smoked with sulphur and juniper instead.

- **Phosphorus and friction matches** [`phosphorus_matches`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/phosphorus_matches.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept medium. The cold fire from urine has been shown at German courts and described by Kunckel (1678); the recipe is a traded secret. It needs barrels of urine and fierce fire.
